When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **1/10** (WATCH, calm price action) vs VIX Spike tier **2/4** (MEDIUM, **60%** probability, skew and backwardation active)
Price has not cracked, but options traders are paying up for downside and for near-term volatility. Trust the VIX Spike for timing risk, because options reprice before price does. Trust the Crash Index for what has actually happened so far.
⚠ These two disagree: Divergence composite zone CALM (**41.9%** of **43** pairs diverging) vs Mother jaws score **100** with six pairs at **80**
The composite averages many quiet pairs and reads calm, while the jaws score flags that a handful of key relationships have broken sharply. Trust the jaws for where stress is building, and the composite for how widespread it is, which is moderate.
⚠ These two disagree: Regime state **27** (STABLE, no regime shift) vs Macro regime CONTRACTION at **40%** confidence with a RISK-OFF bias
The short-term regime score says nothing has shifted yet. The slower macro read says the backdrop is weakening. Trust the macro regime for direction, but at **40%** confidence it deserves a smaller weight than a clean signal would.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The market looks calm on the surface and cautious underneath. The Crash Index sits at 1/10, the regime state scores 27, and the contrarian gauge reads 30, so no extreme sentiment setup is in play. Yet the macro regime is CONTRACTION at 40% confidence and 3 risk-off signals line up. Price says relax. Positioning signals say hold something back.

For positioning, you don't need to cut hard, because no confluence is active (0 of 3). You also have no clean signal to add risk. The sensible stance is to keep exposure where it is, trim the weakest holdings, and keep some cash ready. The Russell 2000 is up +2.7% over 5 days, so the strength is real in small caps. Treat it as something to monitor rather than chase while volatility pricing leans defensive.

The main risk is that VIX Spike moves from tier 2/4 to tier 3/4 while backwardation persists. That would show the protective demand in options is spreading into price. The stance flips toward defense if any of the three confluences (credit stress, small-cap drawdown, yen safe-haven flow) turn active alongside backwardation. It flips back toward risk if backwardation fades and the macro regime confidence rises above 40% in the other direction.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that usually move together are now going different ways. Correlation drift is how much that relationship has changed: a pair that used to move in step (a correlation near +1) now moves apart or in opposite directions (near -1).

The composite zone is CALM, with 41.9% of 43 pairs diverging, 14 bearish, 4 bullish, and a net bias of 10. That is a mild lean to the downside.

The mother jaws score is 100, and six pairs sit at 80 (DEEP DIVERG). Equities and long bonds (SPY vs TLT) went from +0.75 to -0.28.

Semiconductors and the S&P 500 (SMH vs SPY) went from +0.89 to -0.32. Regional banks and financials (KRE vs XLF) went from +0.37 to -0.71, the sharpest shift of the group.

Momentum vs the S&P 500 went from +0.85 to -0.51. Emerging vs developed markets went from +0.90 to -0.05.

AUD/JPY went from +0.55 to -0.33. Regional banks pulling away from the wider financial sector is the pair to watch, because it points to stress that is local rather than general.

When leaders like semiconductors and momentum stocks stop tracking the index, the index is being held up by a narrower group.

Asia · Europe · US · Crypto 24/7 — lead-lag detection
Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Leadership is scattered, and that is a cautious sign. In Asia, the KOSPI (^KS11) leads at +4.8% over 5 days while Hong Kong (^HSI) lags at -2.4%, so the region is not moving together.

Europe is flat: the DAX (^GDAXI) is +0.2% and the Euro Stoxx 50 (^STOXX50E) is -0.6%. In the US, the Russell 2000 (^RUT) leads at +2.7% and the Dow (^DJI) lags at -1.0%, which means small caps are outrunning large industrials.

Crypto trades around the clock and is weak: Bitcoin is -3.8% and Solana is -6.9%, with the riskier coin falling more. Crypto weakness often shows risk appetite fading at the edges before it shows up in stocks.

For the US session, expect small caps to hold their lead unless volatility pricing worsens, and expect large industrial stocks to stay soft. Bitcoin and Solana are the early warning: a further drop in them while the Russell 2000 stalls would mark the point where the small-cap rally loses support.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 1/10 and the VIX Spike at tier 2/4 (MEDIUM, 60% probability) look like a disagreement, but they measure different things. The Crash Index reads what price has already done, and price has been orderly.

The VIX Spike reads what options traders expect next, and they are paying for it: skew is active, meaning downside puts cost more than usual, and backwardation is active, meaning near-term volatility is priced above later months. The adaptive trigger is off, so the signal is not yet at full strength.

This is a coherent state where price is calm and options hedging is rising. Hedging demand like this often comes before moves rather than after them.

Expect the 60% reading to matter most if price starts to slip, because dealers would then have to sell into a market that is already paying up for protection.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
